meta.title: Sweden — Surveillance & Control Architecture
meta.author: Emil Chacon
meta.description: Nine documented surveillance and control measures introduced between 2012 and 2026. Each measure is presented with its official framing and documented aggregate effect. Sources: Swedish state agencies, official propositions, and Lagrådet opinions.

measures.name: Datasparningslag
measures.reality: All internet and telecom metadata retained on all residents. No suspicion required.

measures.name: BankID Dependency
measures.reality: Access to healthcare, banking, tax, schools requires BankID. Loss = civic exclusion.
measures.source: De facto infrastructure — no single law

measures.name: Cashless Infrastructure
measures.reality: All transactions traceable. Anonymous economic participation no longer possible.

measures.name: SIM Card Registration
measures.reality: Anonymous phone use prohibited by law. All devices tied to registered identity.

measures.name: Warrantless Drug Searches
measures.reality: Police may enter homes without warrant on suspicion of drug presence.

measures.name: Preventiva Tvångsmedel (Expanded)
measures.framing: Preventing serious crime before it occurs
measures.reality: Secret surveillance without prior suspicion. 106 court permits issued Q4 2023 alone. All prosecutor offices now authorized.

measures.name: Hemlig Dataavläsning (Permanent)
measures.reality: State-authorized spyware on citizen devices. No time limitation from April 1, 2025.

measures.name: Surveillance of Children Under 15
measures.reality: Secret wiretapping of persons below criminal liability age. Government exceeded its own investigation's recommendations. Nine months faster than proposed.

measures.name: Sverige-id (State e-ID)
measures.reality: National digital identity infrastructure developed and issued by Polismyndigheten. BankID continues alongside — total identity layer now spans private bank + state police.
